title: The trial: Nazarro's witnesses, the phone book and a $5,000 settlement
summary: Nazarro claimed to have taught Buck piano; Bubbles' lawyer used a phone book showing two phones, then settled for $5,000, with fees taking half of the share.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: and he filed the action against Nazarro for neglectment of management and the suit was filed at $150,000; and we had the trial and the Judge as more or less in favor for Buck and Bubbles, because Nazarro tried to prove that he taught Buck how to play the piano, so much that I didn't know how to do nothing and neither one of us knew how to do anything, he did everything. Therefore, he was making his case strong against us and him being who he was and what he was with all the witnesses he had to have against us in his behalf, he had some of the people there like from Lew Leslie's brother, Sal Leslie of the Blackbirds, had him there. They had Lillian Alpert, (phonetic spelling) an agency. Oh, he had several people there that were agents and so forth, they were going to verify his statement against Buck and Bubbles. This is the first time I wished I could have got a piano in the courtroom so the Judge could see Buck play and see what he could have taught him, you know, but I didn't get the piano.

So however, there are two phones in the office, you see, two phones. One for the management and one for the secretary. So the lawyer found out about the phones situation and he went and got a brand new phone book and that's how he won the case. He come to court the next day with a new brief case with this brand new phone book in it. When he got before the Judge and presented his case to the Judge, plus the number in the phone book -- what it was the two phones showed up that this guy was conspiring in some way -- or his secretary was conspiring, that he lost the case. But the Judge told my lawyer, why don't you settle it for four or five thousand dollars. He made this statement to the lawyer. And my lawyer said, I want to go back during recess and talk it over and we'll pick up after.
The lawyer goes to recess and comes back and tells me he says, I think we ought to settle this, how you think you settle? "What's the matter, what are you talking about,

I took this case out to win,lose or draw and I haven't won it and I've lost it and are you afraid of it?" "I'm afraid we might not get --" I said, "Are you afraid of your fee?" I said, "I'm not afraid. But if that's the way you feel, you suit yourself." And he settled it for $5,000. He got $250 and the club then got my $250. That was the end of that.
